column1: # TITLE: Lung adenocarcinoma subtypes definable by lung development-related miRNA expression profiles in association with clinicopathologic features [pre-miRNA analysis - Whole Human Genome 4 x 44K Microarray]
# SUMMARY: Accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes alters regulation of a web of interconnected genes including miRNAs
column2: which confer hallmark capabilities and characteristic cancer features. In this study
column3: the miRNA and mRNA expression profiles of 126 non-small cell lung cancer specimens were analyzed
column4: with special attention given to the diversity of lung adenocarcinomas. Of those
column5: 76 adenocarcinomas were classified into two major subtypes
column7: based on their distinctive miRNA expression profiles resembling those of either developing or adult lungs
column8: respectively. A systems biology-based approach using a Bayesian network and nonparametric regression was employed to estimate the gene regulatory circuitry functioning in patient tumors in order to identify subnetworks enriched for genes with differential expression between the two major subtypes. miR-30d and miR-195
column9: identified as hub genes in such subnetworks
column10: had lower levels of expression in the developing lung-like subtype
column11: while introduction of miR-30d or miR-195 into the lung cancer cell lines evoked shifts of mRNA expression profiles towards the adult lung-like subtype. Conversely
column12: the influence of miR-30d and miR-195 was significantly different between the developing lung- and adult lung-like subtypes in our analysis of the patient dataset. In addition
column14: a child gene of the miR-30d-centered subnetwork
column15: was found to be a direct target of miR-30d. Together
column16: our findings reveal the existence of two miRNA expression profile-defined lung adenocarcinoma subtypes with distinctive clinicopathologic features and also suggest the usefulness of a systems biology-based approach to gain insight into the altered regulatory circuitry involved in cancer development.
